fields.claim: Both builds' control ReceivedBunch needs a 16+ bit first bunch starting with ID 0, whose byte 1 (1 = LE) sets the byte swap; then per message an ID byte and archive reads, passed via vtable +0x18 of [[[channel+0x28]+0x58]+0x208] to NotifyControlMessage

Client packets: handler bits, header word (bits 18-31 sequence, 4-17 acked, 0-3 history words-1, max 8), history, ended by the last byte's top bit. A handshake ack seeds sequences from the cookie; history bits pick ack or nak (lost past 256); nak resends

Client bunch header order: control/open/close, close reason, paused, reliable, packed channel index, 3 flags, reliable sequence, partial bits, conditional channel name, payload bit count; SendRawBunch writes it, sequence (max 1024) and bit count by WriteIntWrapped (fixed widths)

Client FBitReader::SerializeInt(V, Max) reads LSB-first bits with mask 1, 2, 4... while V + mask < Max (none if Max <= 1); SerializeIntPacked reads up to five bytes, each bit 0 a continuation flag and bits 1-7 the next 7-bit group, low group first; the writers mirror them

Client names: a hardcoded bit, then an index (packed from net version 6, else under 411; over 702 rejected; 0 None) or a string, u32 number; Name items via package-map SerializeName; Str strings. Packet info: a bit, a value under 1024, a frame-time bit (receiving client: byte)

Negotiation: the client reads server messages 1, 2, 3, 6, 18, 21, answering Welcome with Netspeed, Challenge with Login. Server Hello: mismatch: Upgrade, close; empty token: Challenge. Login: URL check, PreLogin, Welcome (level, game-mode class and string), login state 2
fields.evidence: static-decompile; M-343, M-344, M-405, M-456, M-457

fields.claim: Client unique-net-id: flags byte (bit 0 encoded, 1 empty, 2 odd, 3-7 type index, 31 then a type name; None ends it, as may 0); encoded, a length byte and that many as uppercase hex (odd drops first digit), else a string; codec rejects stray bits. Challenge (3): a counter-derived string

Client unique-net-id type hashes: 1 NULL, 2 MCP, 3 STEAM, 4 PS4, 6 GOOGLE, 7 GOOGLEPLAY, 8 FACEBOOK, 9 IOS, 10 APPLE, 11 TENCENT, 12 SWITCH, 13 AMAZON, 14 GAMECIRCLE, 15 THUNDERHEAD, 18 Oculus, 19 Quail, 20 PS4SERVER; 5, 16, 17, 21 are runtime FName globals; unknown names hash 0 and hashes None

The client sets its Login response to the literal "0", so Login carries no credential. Both builds hold UTF-16 literals for StatelessConnectHandlerComponent, SteamAuthComponentModuleInterface, PacketHandlerComponents, EncryptionComponent and OnlineSubsystemSteam; their configuration is runtime

The client PDB names PacketHandler's vftable, constructor, Initialize, InitializeComponents, AddHandler, routing and SendHandlerPacket, but no SteamAuthComponent or FSteamAuthComponentModuleInterface vftable, constructor or method: that Steam packet-handler class is not evidenced as linked

SerializeNewActor: actor NetGUID; if dynamic, archetype, flag-gated level, bit-gated location, rotation, scale, velocity: vectors (net version 13+) quantized bit, 3 floats or packed <10,24> ints x 0.1; rotators 3 bit-gated u16s (a x 65536/360)

Client rep layouts: super's replicated properties, then own (field order with class flag 0x80, else offset then name), one per array element; packed handles strictly increase, 0 ends; dynamic arrays a u16 count and nested stream (element (h-1)/N, ending at 0); optional u32 checksums

NetGUIDs (server writes mirror reads): packed GUID (0 null, even nonzero dynamic, recursion max 16); for GUID 1 or exports a flags byte: bit 0 outer GUID and path, then bit 2 a u32 checksum; bit 1 no-load. Original exports set bit 2 without bit 0 (1,641/3,994), no checksum

fields.claim: The fetched 3.0.31 server in the pinned Proton image registers with Steam (secure, game port 17777, auth enabled) once SteamCMD's Linux client libraries sit in its home's .steam/sdk32 and sdk64; without them Steam fails to initialize, as offline

Original data packets start with two clear handler bits (stateless connect, Steam auth) and end with two termination bits (the connection's after the last bunch, then the handler's). Lacking the inner terminator, then the auth bit, both builds reject a packet; with both they accept it

Both builds answer one reliable Hello on the control channel: their own version gets a Challenge (8-unit narrow token) and an ack; another version gets Upgrade carrying theirs, with both values logged. They log their versions as 2406501229 (3.0.31) and 1379612455 (3.0.30), the computed values
